title: Age-Adjusted D-Dimer
sources: Righini M, Van Es J, Den Exter PL, et al. Age-adjusted D-dimer cutoff levels to rule out pulmonary embolism: the ADJUST-PE study. JAMA. 2014;311(11):1117-1124. doi:10.1001/jama.2014.2135

Douma RA, le Gal G, Söhne M, et al. Potential of an age adjusted D-dimer cut-off value to improve the exclusion of pulmonary embolism in older patients: a retrospective analysis of three large cohorts. BMJ. 2010;340:c1475. doi:10.1136/bmj.c1475

Schouten HJ, Geersing GJ, Koek HL, et al. Diagnostic accuracy of conventional or age adjusted D-dimer cut-off values in older patients with suspected venous thromboembolism: systematic review and meta-analysis. BMJ. 2013;346:f2492. doi:10.1136/bmj.f2492

Raja AS, Greenberg JO, Qaseem A, et al. Evaluation of patients with suspected acute pulmonary embolism: best practice advice from the Clinical Guidelines Committee of the American College of Physicians. Ann Intern Med. 2015;163(9):701-711. doi:10.7326/M14-1772
Konstantinides SV, Meyer G, Becattini C, et al. 2019 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of acute pulmonary embolism. Eur Heart J. 2020;41(4):543-603. doi:10.1093/eurheartj/ehz405

American College of Emergency Physicians Clinical Policies Subcommittee on Thromboembolic Disease (Wolf SJ, Hahn SA, Nentwich LM, et al.). Clinical policy: critical issues in the evaluation and management of adult patients presenting to the emergency department with suspected acute venous thromboembolic disease. Ann Emerg Med. 2018;71(5):e59-e109. doi:10.1016/j.annemergmed.2018.03.006

changelog.change: Initial entry — a gap: Wells PE already pointed to an age-adjusted D-dimer that did not exist. Cutoff max(500, age × 10) ng/mL FEU, with the measured value compared against it. All six sources verified against PubMed.

purpose: Raises the D-dimer cutoff for patients over 50 (age × 10 ng/mL instead of 500), so fewer older patients with a non-high pretest probability of PE go to CT. Use only after Wells, revised Geneva, or PERC has placed the patient in the non-high / PE-unlikely group.

inputs.label: D-dimer units (as your lab reports it)

interpretation.label: Age 50 or under: the standard 500 ng/mL cutoff applies
Below the age-adjusted cutoff: D-dimer negative
interpretation.disposition: With a non-high or PE-unlikely pretest probability, PE is excluded: no CT pulmonary angiography. ADJUST-PE 3-month failure rate 0.3% in patients between 500 and their age-adjusted cutoff.

interpretation.label: At or above the cutoff: D-dimer positive
interpretation.disposition: PE is not excluded. Image with CT pulmonary angiography, or V/Q scan if CTPA is contraindicated or unavailable.

notes:
WHO IT IS FOR: patients over 50 with a non-high (revised Geneva) or PE-unlikely (Wells ≤ 4) pretest probability, or low probability that fails PERC. High pretest probability goes straight to imaging; do not order a D-dimer.

UNITS: the studies used the conventional 500 µg/L cutoff, and µg/L equals ng/mL. If your lab reports D-dimer units (DDU) or uses a conventional cutoff other than 500 ng/mL FEU, do not apply this formula; use your laboratory's own age-adjusted guidance.

DO NOT STACK: YEARS was validated without age adjustment, so use one strategy or the other, not both.

EVIDENCE: ADJUST-PE was a prospective management study in emergency department outpatients with suspected PE. In patients 75 and older with a non-high probability, the age-adjusted cutoff raised the share in whom PE could be excluded from 6.4% to 29.7%, with no additional false negatives. For suspected DVT, the support is the Schouten meta-analysis of suspected VTE (sensitivity above 97% in every age group); there is no DVT management study of the same size.
buildNote: Formula engine. max() keeps the 500 floor, so one expression covers every age; the ratio is compared with 1, and rounding to 2 decimals puts 0.995 and above in the positive band.
